text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High GPU queue depth detected in us-west-2 -> pool=prod-gpu-1. Autoscaler failed to add capacity due to repeated driver/runtime errors (CUDA Xid pattern). Root event 3112245600

nisha: paging oncall (i'm oncall) — seeing 80% queue depth and latency spikes, customers getting 500s. can folks gather? :rotating_light:

jake: i'm on it. looking at driver logs now. initial guess: repeated Xid 31/11 OOMs on nodes gpu-node-17..20. attaching tail from dmesg: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=4123, GPU=0: Xid Error
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

alexa: autoscaler tried to request +8 nodes at 3112245660 but cloud API returned quota limit / capacity exhausted. i see concurrent rolling upgrade yesterday 02:00 UTC that bumped drivers on that pool. could be related.

kevin: support reports customers A and B experiencing 15-30s tail latency -> 5xx. I've opened two priority tickets and issued preliminary notice to Customer Success.

marta: what is the blast radius? are non-critical workloads impacted?

jake: blast radius = prod-gpu-1 only. small CPU fallback pool handling a fraction of requests but throughput is down ~60%. Some requests are being retried and piling into the queue.

nisha: immediate mitigations: 1) stop scheduling new jobs to afflicted nodes 2) divert traffic to warmpool and CPU fallback 3) attempt driver restart on healthy nodes 4) create incident channel and inform customers. i'll coordinate.

alexa: doing `kubectl get nodes -l pool=prod-gpu-1 -o wide` -> nodes 17..24. i'm going to cordon/drain nodes 17-20 one at a time to prevent more failures.

jake: +1. before drain, we should taint nodes to prevent new pods from starting: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-17 gpu-unhealthy=true:NoSchedule`

alexa: taint applied, starting cordon+drain on gpu-node-17. draining pods that can tolerate eviction. forcing graceful timeout 120s for critical ones.

incident-bot: deploy-bot reports: recent driver rollout 3112150000 -> drivers/kernel module version nv-510.9 applied to prod-gpu-1 during maintenance window.

jake: that aligns. logs show driver module unloading errors during warmup. I want to roll back the driver to nv-495 on these nodes and hold. Can we rollback via the node image in the pool?

alexa: cloud images have previous image snap-495. I can trigger a replace-node action for nodes 17-20 to spin up nodes with snap-495, then drain old ones. This takes ~10-12 min per node.

marta: customer comms: Kevin, please send an update that we're investigating GPU capacity issues causing degraded throughput and that we're diverting workload and escalating. ETA next update in 30m.

kevin: on it. short note posted to customers: "We're investigating degraded performance for model inferencing in us-west-2. We've detected GPU driver instability and are performing mitigations. We'll update in 30 minutes."

jake: small experiment: on gpu-node-21 (healthy) i'm going to restart the nvidia-driver daemon to recreate kernel modules: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` -> watching for Xid reappearance.

(alexa): drain done for node-17. starting node replace for node-17 -> launching instance with snap-495.

incident-bot: autoscaler: scale request queued at 3112245780 -> failed due to cloud quota limit: "Insufficient capacity: requested 8 g4dn.xlarge"

jake: because autoscaler is blocked, we need to temporarily enable degraded-serving fallback: switch route weight to CPU fallback pool for latency-sensitive customers. Nisha, can you approve?

nisha: approve. do it. also enable retry budgets to reduce retry storms.

alexa: rerouted traffic. CPU fallback now handling ~28% of traffic previously on GPU. Latency for those requests is higher but stable.

kevin: customers A/B notified. CS updated.

jake: quick health check: nodes 18-20 still showing Xid bursts when any new GPU workload starts; suspect memory leak in kernel driver. I'm preparing a hotpatch: adjust `nvidia-modeset` module parameter to reduce memory usage and restart. This is risky; prefer node replacement to older image.

marta: what's impact if we keep replacing nodes sequentially? how long until pool capacity recovers?

alexa: if replacements maintain pace, we can restore ~50% capacity in 90 minutes, full capacity in ~6 hours. But cloud quota may still block autoscale beyond pool size.

nisha: escalation decision: 1) do sequential node replacement to older driver image 2) open quota request with cloud (already started) 3) schedule oncall handoff in 2 hours to Jake (overnight) 4) post incident notice to status page.

incident-bot: incident created INC-2026-31122456. Pager duty acknowledged by nisha.

kevin: status page update posted: "Investigating GPU driver instability causing service degradation in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress. Next update in 30m."

jake: replace completed for node-17 and 18 -> both back in service on snap-495 and passing health checks. queue depth dropped ~18% after node-18 came back.

alexa: node-19 replacement in progress. drain complete. spin-up time longer than expected due to image pull.

kevin: a subset of customer requests still getting 502s intermittently; looks correlated with remaining patched nodes. customers asking for ETA.

jake: ETA: continuing replacements, estimating incremental recovery: next 30m should see another 20% improvement. monitor for Xid reappearance; if it reappears on snap-495 we escalate to kernel driver vendor.

marta: are we blocking any safety-critical workflows? any legal/regulation customers affected?

kevin: no safety-critical. a regulated customer reported slower response but no data exposure.

nisha: handoff: i'm handing to jake for overnight watch at 3132273400 (two hours). Jake — please maintain node replacements, keep status updates cadence, and if Xid appears on snap-495 escalate to eng-ml and vendor.

jake: acknowledged. will keep runbook and roll logs in the incident channel. also adding a temporary rule to the scheduler to prefer warm nodes.

incident-bot: Pager duty: next oncall (jake) has been notified for handoff at 3112262800.

alexa: postmortem notes to capture: driver rollout correlation, autoscaler not permitted to scale due to cloud quota, insufficient warmpool capacity, need preflight checks for driver rollouts on critical pools, add automatic fallback route to avoid retry storms.

kevin: final customer update queued for 30m with current mitigation steps and ETA window.

nisha: closing immediate P0 reactive steps. monitoring. incident remains open for replacement completion and vendor follow-up. :white_check_mark:

jake: logging all commands and logs to INC-2026-31122456. I'll ping if Xid recurs.

deploy-bot: rollback job triggered for driver-rollout-prod-gpu-1 -> job 3112246001 queued.

alexa: node-19 came back healthy; node-20 still pending replacement. queue depth now down to 35% and error rate reduced by ~70% from peak.

kevin: customer update sent: "We have restored most capacity by rolling back the recent driver update on affected nodes and diverting traffic. We will follow up with a full post-incident report."

nisha: thanks team. we'll reconvene for postmortem tomorrow 13:00 UTC. documenting next steps in INC-2026-31122456.

(End of thread)
